meaning: A design in which an encoder turns both the context and the target into latents and a predictor is trained to output the target's latent from the context's, so the loss never compares pixels.
The network that turns what the camera saw into latent vectors.
The second network of a JEPA: it takes the latents of what was seen (and, in a world model, an action) and outputs a guess at the target latents.
A learned summary vector of a frame or part of one; papers also call it a representation or an embedding.
The distance between a predicted latent and a target or goal latent: low when the two are a plausible match.
A transformer that reads a picture as a sequence of patches, one token per patch.
A small square of an image, 16 by 16 pixels in V-JEPA 2.
A patch extended through time: the same square in 2 consecutive frames, which becomes one token.
One element of the sequence a transformer processes; here a vector made from one tubelet of pixels.
Removing tokens before the encoder sees them, so the model has to predict the latents of what was hidden.
A learned placeholder vector, tagged with a position, that tells the predictor to output the latent that belongs there.
The encoder copy that sees only the visible tokens and is trained by the loss.
The encoder copy that sees the whole clip and supplies the answers; it is updated by an EMA and receives no gradient.
Subtract two lists of numbers entry by entry, drop the signs and add up (or average).
An instruction to treat a value as a constant during training, so no weight behind it is changed by the loss.
A running average in which recent values count most; the target encoder's weights are an EMA of the context encoder's.
The fraction of its old value a target weight keeps at each EMA update; 0.99925 in V-JEPA 2.
The shortcut in which the encoder maps every input to the same latent, which zeroes the loss and makes the latents useless.
A partial collapse in which latents differ but only inside a thin slice of the space, so most of their numbers carry nothing.

expansion: named after its terms: variance, invariance, covariance
meaning: A 2022 method that blocks collapse with loss terms that keep every latent dimension spread out and uncorrelated with the others.
A loss term that pushes a batch of latents toward a round Gaussian cloud by testing its projections on random directions.
A bell-shaped cloud with the same spread in every direction and no correlation between dimensions.
Latents of different inputs that a loss term pushes apart to block collapse; an older method.
A pretrained encoder whose weights are not changed while a predictor is trained on top of it.
Meta's video JEPA of 2025: an encoder pretrained on video by masked latent prediction.
The V-JEPA 2 predictor trained on robot video to predict the next frame's latents from the current latents, the gripper state and an action.
The March 2026 successor encoder family, trained with a revised recipe and offered up to 2B parameters.
An October 2026 robot world model: action-conditioned predictors up to 8B parameters on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder.
A JEPA world model of about 15M parameters that trains encoder and predictor together and blocks collapse with SIGReg.
A JEPA world model that trains its encoder with variance and covariance terms; named here as the LeWorldModel authors' comparison.
A latent world model built on a frozen pretrained image encoder.
A picture of the desired end state; its latent is what the planner tries to reach.
How many predictor steps ahead a planner imagines for each candidate.
Plan a sequence of actions through a model, execute only the first part, observe, and plan again.
A search that samples candidate action sequences from a Gaussian, keeps the lowest-cost few and refits the Gaussian to them, round after round.
The lowest-cost candidates of a CEM round, used to refit the sampling distribution.
One forward run of the predictor for one candidate and one step; samples x iterations x horizon passes are needed per decision.
A simulated 2D pushing task used as a benchmark for small world models.
